steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed.
Put the ignition in ON/RUN without starting the engine.
Press the up or down arrow on the steering wheel until Vehicle Info shows in the cluster display.
Press the left or right arrow to scroll through the Vehicle Info screens to Oil Life.
Press and hold OK until the oil life gauge and number go back to 100%.
Start the engine and check that the oil change message is gone.
oil.note: The reset only works when the conditions are met (engine off, ignition on). If the message is back at the next start, repeat the steps.

oil.when: 2024 Wrangler with push-button start (accelerator pedal method)
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed.
Keep your foot off the brake and press ENGINE START/STOP so the ignition is in ON/RUN. Do not start the engine.
Slowly push the accelerator pedal all the way to the floor and let it up, three times, all within ten seconds.
Start the engine. If the oil change message shows again, the reset did not take, so repeat the steps.
oil.note: The 2024 handbook says the message can also be reset from the instrument cluster display menu.

oil.when: 2013 Wrangler and Wrangler Unlimited with a turn key (accelerator pedal method)
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the key to ON/RUN without starting the engine.
Push the accelerator pedal all the way to the floor three times within 10 seconds.
Turn the key back to OFF/LOCK.
Start the engine and check that the change oil message is gone. If it is still there, repeat the steps.

tpms.when: 2013 Wrangler and Wrangler Unlimited (no reset button; the light clears itself)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the sticker in the driver's door opening, and check the spare too.
Drive normally. After the tires are filled, it can take up to about 20 minutes of driving before the light turns off by itself.
tpms.note: The 2013 guide says the light can flash when a tire is low and may take up to 20 minutes of driving to go out after the tire is filled. If it does not go out, or keeps coming back, have the tires and the system checked.
